text: Liu et al. (2011, Nature) developed a framework for identifying the minimum set of 'driver nodes' needed to fully control a network's dynamical state -- a concept later linked to reprogramming factors such as the Yamanaka factors. What computational method did they use to find this minimum driver set?
choices: A maximum matching algorithm applied to the network's directed graph structure
Random forest regression trained on single-cell expression profiles
Mutual information filtering using the Data Processing Inequality
Quasi-steady-state relaxation of a Boolean network into a continuous sigmoidal model
explanation: Liu et al. used maximum matching on the network's directed graph to identify the minimum set of driver nodes needed for full structural controllability, and observed that known cell-reprogramming factors often correspond to these driver nodes. Choice 1 describes GENIE3-style GRN inference, and choice 2 describes ARACNE -- both infer network structure from data rather than analyze controllability of a known structure. Choice 3 describes the SQUAD approach for converting Boolean models to continuous ones, an unrelated technique.
